wikiGoal: A code wiki for this repository.

pages.title: Data model, migrations, and delete semantics
pages.purpose: Document the SQLite schema, how migrations are embedded and applied at startup, the FTS virtual table, and the cascade/nullify behavior every write path depends on.
instructions: Document enforced vs. hand-written referential behavior: deletes in repositories explicitly null out items.category_id/container_id and children parent_id before deleting the row, item delete cascades item_images/item_tags/item_documents rows but only removes image files from disk (PDFs and orphaned thumbs can survive) — verify against code when editing.
Explain the FTS table as a derived projection, including why 0003 drops and recreates items_fts to add location_note.
Explain the migration workflow: sqlx::migrate! embeds server/migrations at compile time and runs on every startup, so schema change = new numbered file + rebuild; never edit an applied migration.
Include a mermaid ER diagram: categories/containers self-referencing trees, items, item_images, item_documents, tags/item_tags, and items_fts.
Note conventions: UUID string ids, TEXT timestamps via datetime('now'), no compile-time sqlx query checking.

pages.title: HTTP API surface, DTO semantics, and error contract
pages.purpose: Canonical route table plus the request/response conventions a caller or endpoint author must follow: extractors, DTO field semantics, pagination clamps, upload limits, and the JSON error envelope.
instructions: Call out the non-obvious update semantics in repositories/item.rs: for UpdateItem and UpdateContainer, omitted Option fields overwrite with NULL (description/purchased_at/bought_from/price/category_id/container_id) while name/source_type fall back to existing values — a partial payload can clear data.
Document the error contract: AppError variants to 404/400/500, JSON body { "error": string }, internal errors are logged but masked, and sqlx RowNotFound maps to 404.
Enumerate every route registered in routes.rs with method, path, handler, and the request/response DTO types — this table is the reference other pages should link to instead of duplicating.
Keep web-side wiring out of this page; link to integrations/frontend-backend-contract.
Record pagination behavior (page ≥ 1, size clamped 1..=100, defaults 1/20) and that list endpoints return { items, total, page, size }.
Record upload constraints: multipart field name must be `file`; global DefaultBodyLimit is 100MB; image size capped by upload.max_file_size, PDF by upload.max_doc_size.

pages.title: System shape and runtime domains
pages.purpose: Explain the deployed shape — one Rust binary that owns the REST API, the embedded SPA, uploaded media, and SQLite — and the runtime domains/layering a change must respect.
instructions: Capture the intended layering routes.rs → handlers → {repositories, services} → models and note the real dependency pattern: handlers call repositories directly and use services only for image storage + FTS sync, so 'services layer' is thin.

Describe the four runtime domains served by one process: /api/v1 JSON API, /images (ServeDir over image_dir), /docs (ServeDir over docs_dir), and the fallback SPA embedded from web/dist via rust-embed.
Include a mermaid diagram of the process, its routers/services, and the SQLite + filesystem backing it.
Note module inventory at a high level only; do not mirror the source tree file by file.

pages.title: Uploads, on-disk layout, and served URL contract
pages.purpose: Map stored relative paths to served URLs for images and PDF documents, and record the upload/thumbnail/delete pipeline plus its current gaps (orphan files, dev-proxy mismatch).
instructions: Document save_image details: allowed extensions in code (jpg/jpeg/png/webp/avif), max-size check on the buffered bytes, id-based filenames, 300px thumbnail, jpeg→jpg normalization, and the avif branch that returns the original as its own thumb.

Document the URL contract and where it is enforced: DB stores subdir-relative paths, server nest_service('/images', image_dir) and '/docs', SPA prefixes '/images/' and '/docs/pdf/'; note that Vite's dev proxy only forwards /api and /data/images, so media URLs are not proxied in dev — verify before assuming media works under `pnpm dev`.
Flag that AGENTS.md/nginx comments still describe a /data/images prefix that no longer matches the code, and note deletion gaps: deleting an item removes image files but not stored PDF files.
Include a mermaid diagram of upload → disk → DB row → browser URL for one image and one PDF.

Lay out the storage contract: images at {image_dir}/items/{uuid}.{ext} + {uuid}_thumb.{ext}, containers at {image_dir}/containers/ (single image_path column, no thumb recorded), PDFs at {docs_dir}/pdf/{uuid}.pdf.

pages.title: Hierarchies, container paths, and location modeling
pages.purpose: Explain how the two trees (categories, containers) are stored, assembled, rendered, and destroyed, and how an item's 'where' is derived from the container ancestor chain.
instructions: Cover the UI-side equivalents: flattenTree producing indented <Select> options with ancestor path labels, containerPathText falling back to "未归位".
Document build_tree (flat rows → nested nodes, name-sorted, orphans become roots) in both repositories and why list_tree is computed in Rust rather than SQL.
Document get_path: iterative parent walk, reversed root→leaf, and how the same PathSegment[] is reused for container breadcrumbs, item '位置', and search hits.
Note that category rename affects display but not the FTS index — cross-link the search page rather than re-deriving.

Record delete semantics (nullify children and item references, not cascade) and container_type vocabulary (frontend offers room/table/shelf/box/drawer/cabinet/bag/other while the DB default is 'other').

pages.title: Full-text search and FTS index synchronization
pages.purpose: The search subsystem's contract: trigram FTS5 index contents, the LIKE fallback for short queries, snippet/highlight assembly, and exactly which writes keep the index fresh (and which silently don't).
instructions: Document query planning in repositories/search.rs: queries with fewer than 3 chars use LIKE over item/container/category columns, otherwise MATCH with the query wrapped in double quotes; snippet() spans columns 1–3; highlight joins marked snippets or falls back to a truncated description.

Explain sync points precisely from code: item create/update call sync_item in the handler, item delete removes the FTS row directly, and sync_all runs (best-effort, warn-only) on every startup — there are no triggers.
Explain the index shape: items_fts with tokenize='trigram' (CJK support), indexed columns name/description/location_note/tags/container_name/container_label/category_name, item_id UNINDEXED.

State the drift invariant loudly: tag rename/delete and container/category rename do not resync affected items, so search can lag until restart; if a change touches those writes, consider calling sync_item for linked items.
Use a mermaid flow diagram for the search request decision and highlight assembly; keep the UI rendering contract (dangerouslySetInnerHTML on <mark> output) explicit.

pages.title: Source of truth, generated files, and documentation drift
pages.purpose: Give an agent the repo's conventions and the known places where prose docs disagree with code, so it edits the right file instead of trusting stale guidance.
instructions: Document generated files that must never be hand-edited: web/src/routeTree.gen.ts (TanStack router plugin), web/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, Cargo.lock (regenerate via cargo) and web/pnpm-lock.yaml.

List concrete drift observed today: AGENTS.md says images are served at /data/images with data/images/... DB paths (code uses /images + subdir-relative paths), claims components/ui is empty scaffolding (real components exist), and claims no CI (an OpenWiki GitHub workflow exists); docs/design.md lists nonexistent files (App.tsx, many components) and triggers-based FTS sync.
Note the OpenWiki workflow regenerates this wiki on a schedule; do not hand-edit generated pages when a source-doc change is the real fix.
Record product conventions: UI copy is Chinese, source_type vocabulary (purchased/handmade/gift/salvage/other), '未归位' for unassigned items, description rendered as Markdown.
State the precedence order: code (server/src, web/src, migrations) > justfile/deploy > README > AGENTS.md > docs/design.md (partly aspirational).

pages.title: Frontend ↔ backend integration contract
pages.purpose: The runtime wiring between the React SPA and the Rust API: fetch wrapper and error mapping, React Query hooks and cache invalidation keys, multipart calls, generated router file, and what to touch when the API or a route changes.
instructions: Add an 'API change checklist': Rust model in server/src/models → handler/repository → web/src/types/index.ts → web/src/lib/api.ts → hook invalidation → affected route components.

Document the React Query layer: query keys (['items', params], ['items', id], ['containers', ...], ['search', params], ['stats'], ['tags'], ['categories']) and which hooks invalidate which keys on mutation success — this is where stale-UI bugs come from.
Document the client: BASE '/api/v1', JSON request helper that throws Error(body.error || statusText), and the raw fetch multipart helpers for image/document upload that bypass the JSON header.

Explain provider/router setup in main.tsx and that routeTree.gen.ts is generated by @tanstack/router-plugin from web/src/routes (never hand-edited; bare layout routes such as items/$id.tsx render an Outlet).
Note the hardcoded /images/ and /docs/pdf/ URL prefixes and the dev-proxy mismatch as a cross-boundary risk (link, don't duplicate, file-storage-and-url-contract).

pages.title: Build, dev loop, and the embedded-SPA constraint
pages.purpose: How to build and run the two halves, why a frontend change requires rebuilding the Rust binary, and which commands are authoritative versus stale documentation.
instructions: Do not repeat deployment topologies here.
Document the recipe set from justfile: deps, dev/dev-server/dev-web, build, run, install/uninstall, container-*, test, fmt, lint, check, clean, reset-db, and the default ports (3000 API, 5173 Vite).

Explain the build dependency: rust-embed reads ../web/dist at compile time, so `cargo build` without a fresh web/dist embeds stale or missing assets; just build handles this by touching server/src/main.rs after a frontend rebuild.
Note AGENTS.md drift (it claims no CI/lint config and root-relative data/ defaults); prefer justfile + code, and link the drift page.
State the run-from-repo-root requirement and that missing web/dist breaks compilation of static_files.rs.

pages.title: Configuration, data directories, and upload limits
pages.purpose: Explain every knob that changes runtime behavior — config.toml/CONFIG_PATH, CLI overrides, XDG-derived default paths, and size parsing — plus the fact that config is re-read per request.
instructions: Document parse_size (digit prefix + KB/MB/GB, unknown unit treated as MB) and that uploads are validated in handlers/services, while the global axum body limit is a fixed 100MB in main.rs.
Document resolution order: CONFIG_PATH or ./config.toml if it exists, else Default impl, then CLI --host/--port/--help overrides; unknown args exit(1).
Document the full TOML shape: [server] host/port, [data] db_path/image_dir/docs_dir, [upload] max_file_size (default 10MB) and max_doc_size (default 50MB, serde default).
Explain the default data dir: $XDG_DATA_HOME/wheremystuff, else $HOME/.local/share/wheremystuff, else ./data — note this contradicts README's 'creates data/ in the current directory' claim.

Flag that Config::load() is invoked inside individual handlers (item/container upload and delete paths), so config/env/CLI state is consulted per request rather than once at startup — relevant to any caching or test-isolation change.

pages.title: Deployment: systemd, Podman, and nginx
pages.purpose: Describe the three supported deployment paths and the packaging constraints they impose, including volume/path mismatches that break persistence if copied verbatim.
instructions: Cover each artifact concretely: 3-stage Containerfile (node frontend → rust backend with --from=frontend web/dist → debian-slim runtime with only the binary and WORKDIR /app), systemd unit hardening (ProtectSystem, ReadWritePaths on %h/.local/share/wheremystuff), and nginx proxy (client_max_body_size 20M, / proxy_pass, optional static image location).
Flag the nginx commented block still referencing /data/images, which no longer matches the /images route served by main.rs.

Flag the persistence mismatch: the container declares VOLUME /app/data and just container-run mounts ./data, but with no config.toml the default data dir resolves via HOME to ~/.local/share/wheremystuff inside the container — verify before documenting 'data persists in ./data'.
Include the upgrade procedure (rebuild frontend + binary, restart service/container) and note migrations run automatically on startup, so no separate migration step exists.
Keep port/upload-limit basics linked to configuration rather than duplicated.

pages.title: Testing and validation playbook
pages.purpose: What automated coverage exists (almost none), which gates actually run, and how to verify each class of change manually against a real server and database.
instructions: Give change-specific checklists: new migration (startup applies it + FTS resync), search behavior change (test <3 char and ≥3 char queries, CJK, tag/container renames), upload change (size limit, extension rejection, thumbnail presence), frontend route change (regenerate routeTree, tsc, embedded build).
List the real gates: cargo clippy -p server -- -D warnings, prettier --check on web/src, tsc -b with strict/noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters, and pnpm build (tsc -b && vite build).
Note there is no seed/fixture data or reset automation beyond `just reset-db`, which deletes data/ only — not the XDG path used by installed builds.

Provide a manual verification matrix with concrete curl/fetch recipes: API smoke (GET /api/v1/stats, CRUD item, GET /search?q=), upload checks against temp dirs, and how to point the server at an isolated DB via CONFIG_PATH to avoid touching real data.
State plainly that server/tests is empty, no test targets exist, and dev-dependencies (reqwest, tempfile) are unused — `just test` / `cargo test -p server` passes trivially today.

pages.title: Workflow: browse and manage containers, categories, and tags
pages.purpose: Trace the tree browsing and management flows (container tree → detail → children/items → edit/delete/parent change) and the category/tag admin screens, including what each mutation does to items and search.
instructions: Cover category create/edit/delete with parent selection and tag CRUD + autocomplete (limit 10, prefix LIKE), noting tags.name UNIQUE and idempotent create.
Document editing: inline EditContainerForm, parent selection from the flattened tree via PUT /containers/{id}, child creation, and post-delete navigation to parent or /containers.
Document the delete consequences visible to users (items become 未归位, children become roots) and the search-staleness consequence (container name/label no longer matches items until re-sync).

Include a mermaid flow for container detail: GET /containers/{id} composes container + path + direct children + up to 100 items (item::list with size 100), so 'all items under a container' means direct children only.
Note that POST /containers/{id}/image exists server-side but has no SPA caller — relevant if a task asks to add container photos.

pages.title: Workflow: create, edit, and enrich an item
pages.purpose: Trace the end-to-end item write path from the form through API, tags, image upload, FTS sync, and cache invalidation, and list the invariants a change to this flow must preserve.
instructions: Call out the update-field-clearing pitfall from the API semantics and the fact that tag changes are the path that keeps FTS correct for tags (unlike tag rename elsewhere).
Document tag creation via POST /tags being idempotent by name (returns the existing tag), and that attaching tags happens through item.tag_ids (set_tags replaces the whole set).
Document the edit page's local-state hydration effect, image delete through DELETE /items/{id}/images/{image_id}, and document upload through the DocumentList component.

Highlight the multi-step, non-transactional nature: item row is committed before images upload, each upload is its own request, and a failed upload leaves the item without that image; describe the resulting partial states.
Include a mermaid sequence diagram: form submit → POST/PUT /items → repository insert/update + set_tags → sync_item → response ItemDetail → sequential image uploads → navigate to detail.

pages.title: Workflow: search from query to location
pages.purpose: Follow a user query from the home/search page through the search endpoint into results rendering, and spell out the paging, highlighting, and staleness behaviors that tests or fixes must consider.
instructions: Explain URL-as-state: search terms and page live in TanStack Router search params, so changing the input alone does not refetch until submit/navigate.
Keep the index-maintenance rules on the search concept page and link to it; here cover only the request/response path and UI behaviors (loading skeletons, empty state, pagination links).
Note the per-row N+1 ancestor walk in get_path and the ranking difference (ORDER BY rank vs created_at DESC) as performance/behavior observations, not mandates.

Use a mermaid sequence/flow diagram covering route search params (q, page) → useSearch (disabled for empty q) → GET /search → FTS vs LIKE branch → container_path enrichment per row → highlight → render.

pages.title: Quickstart — wheremystuff (东西在哪)
pages.purpose: Orientation hub for the repo: what the app does, how the Rust API + React SPA fit together, the minimal dev loop, and a task→page routing map so a coding agent can jump straight to the right subsystem.
instructions: Include a task-routing table (e.g. 'add an API field', 'change search', 'change upload limits', 'deploy', 'new DB column') mapping to the specific wiki page and the owning source files.
Link, do not restate: architecture/overview, workflows, operations, integrations, testing.
Mention the hard operational constraint that the binary must be run from the repo root and that the SPA is embedded at compile time (frontend change ⇒ rebuild).
State the repo's source-of-truth rule: server/src and web/src win over AGENTS.md and docs/design.md, which are partially stale/aspirational; point to the drift page instead of repeating details.
This is the init entry page; keep it short and make it a router, not a tutorial dump.
